items.bold: RUBIO: US expects Iran response "TODAY." Trump: expecting letter from Iran "supposedly tonight." Iran FM: "grotesque absurdity."
items.text: CNBC (20 hours ago) confirmed: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Friday morning that the US expects to receive a response from Iran on its peace proposal "today." items.bold: FRIDAY: Iran fired missiles at UAE AGAIN. US struck TWO EMPTY Iranian tankers evading blockade. Rubio: IRGC agency "unacceptable."
items.text: CNBC and DD India confirmed: Iran fired missiles at the UAE on Friday for the second consecutive day. The UAE Defence Ministry said its air defenses engaged two ballistic missiles and three drones launched from Iran. The US fired on two empty Iranian oil tankers on Friday that were trying to evade the naval blockade. Iran's military said US forces targeted an Iranian oil tanker, a second ship, and civilian areas in the strait and on the mainland. Secretary Rubio said Friday: "We've seen a report overnight that Iran has established, or trying to establish, some agency that's going to control traffic in the straits. That would be a problem. That would actually be unacceptable." Rubio also confirmed the latest US military action was "separate and distinct from Operation Epic Fury" — defensive in nature. Ceasefire formally in effect but severely strained.

assessment.body:
Saturday 6:00 PM IST. Day 71. The world is waiting for Iran's letter.

THE DIPLOMATIC MOMENT
• Rubio: US expects Iran response "today" (Friday)
• Trump: expecting a letter from Iran "supposedly tonight"
• Iran FM: "grotesque absurdity" to seek peace while proposing "one big glow"
• The Iran letter — if it arrives this weekend — is the most consequential diplomatic document of the 71-day war
• It will determine: deal or resumed strikes

THE FRIDAY MILITARY PICTURE
• Iran fired missiles at UAE Friday — second consecutive day
• UAE air defenses engaged 2 ballistic missiles + 3 drones
• US fired on two empty Iranian oil tankers evading blockade
• Iran: US targeted tankers, a second ship, and "civilian areas"
• Ceasefire: formally in effect per Trump/Rubio — but violated daily by both sides

THE CHINA DIMENSION — COMPLICATED
• US sanctioned Chinese companies over Iran links — days before Trump-Xi Beijing
• This complicates the Hormuz pressure track: China being sanctioned + asked to pressure Iran simultaneously
• CNN sources: Mojtaba Khamenei personally shaping Iran's war strategy
• Khamenei in direct oversight = any deal needs his personal approval

THE RUBIO RED LINE
• Rubio: Iran's IRGC vetting agency is "unacceptable"
• This directly confronts Iran's permanent Hormuz architecture
• NASA satellite confirms Omani lane deserted and under attack
• IRGC toll agency formalised — Rubio says "a problem"
• Gap: Iran wants permanent Hormuz control; US says unacceptable

INDIA'S WEEKEND
• Weekly: Sensex +0.5%, Nifty +0.7% — net positive from Wednesday MOU rally
• Friday: Sensex -516, Nifty -151. SBI -6.6%. BSE cap -Rs 1.5T
• Brent $101 — holding near $100 psychological level
• Rupee ~Rs 94-94.50 — stable per Geojit analysis
• Kharif fertiliser: May 10-12 last viable restart window
• Iran letter BINARY for Monday open

VERDICT: Day 71 is the most diplomatically consequential weekend of the 71-day West Asia War. Iran's Supreme Leader Khamenei — now confirmed to be personally shaping war strategy — must decide whether to send a letter that accepts the US framework, modifies it, or rejects it. Every word of that letter will move Brent by $5-10, Sensex by 500-1,500 points, and determine whether India's kharif season is salvageable. The world — and India's 1.4 billion people — are waiting for a letter from Tehran.

featured.title: The Strait of Hormuz and the New Logic of Chokepoint Control
featured.desc: Chokepoint control is no longer binary (open/closed) but a layered spatial contest spanning seabed topology, island sovereignty, electronic warfare, and visibility asymmetry. The cartography of maritime control in the 2026 crisis.

featured.title: Geopolitics of LPG Supply in India
featured.desc: How India's LPG import dependency on the Gulf creates acute vulnerability during the West Asia War. Explores Hormuz exposure, alternative supply routes, and policy imperatives for energy security in a blockade scenario.

featured.title: Geopolitics of Fertiliser Supply in India
featured.desc: India imports 30%+ of its fertilisers via the Strait of Hormuz. This paper maps the supply chain risks to kharif and rabi crops, the strategic case for diversification, and what a prolonged blockade means for food security.
